chapter_theme: The search for the head and feet (அடிமுடி தேடல்): when Brahma and Vishnu each claim to be the Lord, Siva stands before them as a boundless column of fire whose crown and feet neither can find; he is flesh, life and awareness and beyond sun and moon, and is reached not by those who worship for gifts but by those who give themselves to him.
structure_note: The quarrel and the fire (372, 373), Siva as all and beyond all (374), the failed search (375, 376), Brahma and Vishnu within his nature (377), the linga and the true path (378), and the contrast between gods who seek gifts and devotees who reach his feet (379, 380).

372.reading: When Brahma and Mal, through their own folly, each said 'I am the Lord', the Supreme stood before them spread out as fire, and they searched for Hara's feet and cried out.
372.nuance: பேதைமை (folly) is named as the cause of the claim, not of the search. அரற்றுகின்றார் (cry out, lament) ends the verse on their helplessness rather than on any finding.

373.reading: While they said 'we stand filling the seven worlds', the Lord himself stood as a mass of flame through the seven worlds; I came to know him, the great-gem-throated one who fills the seven heavens, by his own might.
373.nuance: The first line may be the two gods' boast. The variant last line, நானே அறிந்தேன் என் ஆண்மையினாலே (I knew him by my own power), reverses the sense: the text makes knowledge of Siva his gift, the variant the knower's achievement. With the text, the speaker succeeds where the gods' self-claim failed.

374.reading: As flesh, as life, as awareness and as fire, as the far heaven and as the holy form of the gods' fire, he passed beyond the pillar of the universe, the sun and the cool moon, and stood as the whole universe that he rules.
374.nuance: The verse moves from the body (ஊன்) outward to the cosmos, so that Siva is at once in the flesh and beyond the sun and moon. தாணு means pillar and is also a name of Siva; here it may be the axis of the cosmos.

375.reading: He stood, the tall one, through all the earth and the universe; then the two who sought out his form were afraid; one went up toward the holy crown, and the good anklet-feet could not be found either.
375.nuance: அஞ்சினர் (they feared) adds what the story often leaves out: the search ends in fear, not just failure. Tradition has Brahma fly up as a swan and Vishnu dig down as a boar; the verse names neither.

376.reading: The gods close in devotion who praise his red feet, the one who asked for three steps, the sages, and Brahma who makes the worlds by verse: this is how they stride and come to bow their heads.
376.nuance: The verse plays on அடி (foot, step, metrical foot): சேவடி, மூவடி (Vamana's three steps), பாவடி, தாவடி. பாவடியாலே பதஞ்செய் பிரமன் may mean Brahma who creates by Vedic verse. The last line is read as the great at last bowing to Siva's feet; it may also be ironic.

377.reading: The four-faced one seated in the lotus and the lord who dwells in the dark sea both share the nature of that great being, who is sensed within the body as its life.
377.nuance: The syntax could equally say that Brahma and Vishnu are of his nature, or that they abide within it. The variant கடலூழித் தலைவன் (lord of the sea at the aeon's end) changes the epithet for Vishnu. The image of life felt within flesh brings the cosmic Lord inside the body.

378.reading: The supreme light that rose as an embrace set here a true path above; seeing it, the world embraces it and circles it, and grace may be gained by those who turn to it.
378.nuance: ஆலிங்கனம் (embrace) puns on இலிங்கம் (linga); the verse is traditionally read as the column of fire becoming the linga that the world worships by circling. முங்கண் (three eyes, or 'the front') and கோலிங்கமைஞ்சு are obscure.

379.reading: The gods who worshipped the one who gave the sword do not know Hara as we do who gave ourselves to him; they will not reach the feet of him who took us as his own, gave us joy and gave us his feet to hold.
379.nuance: ஆள்கொடுத்து is used twice: the devotees give themselves (become his servants), and he takes them as his own. The gods worship for a gift (the sword given to Brahma) and so stay outside; the contrast is between worship for boons and self-giving.

380.reading: To the one who circled through the aeon and asked of him, the four-faced one comes forth and appears; when he said 'give what was ordained, the water from the fallen head', he outshone the light of the sun at the aeon's end.
380.nuance: The verse is obscure. ஊழி வலஞ்செய்து echoes 349, where Brahma and Vishnu circle Siva through the aeon, and வீழித் தலைநீர் may refer to the Ganga from Siva's head or to the skull of Brahma. Only the close is clear: Siva's light surpasses the sun of the final dissolution.

links.note: The Kural defines folly as the pride that says 'we are bright'; Tirumular shows it at the top of the cosmos, Brahma and Vishnu each saying 'I am the Lord' through folly (பேதைமை), and failing before the fire.
349 records Siva's giving the sword to Brahma and the discus to Vishnu; 379 judges such gifts: the gods who worship the giver of the sword do not reach his feet, as those who give themselves do.
Both open on circling through the aeon (ஊழி வலஞ்செய்): in 349 Brahma and Vishnu circle Siva and receive weapons, in 380 one who circles is answered as Siva outshines the sun of dissolution.

373 sets the two gods' failure against the speaker's claim: நானே அறிந்தேன் அவனாண்மையாலே, I knew him by his might. Arunagiri names the same Siva whom Brahma and Vishnu could not find (அரிதான), the fire filling the sky, and asks whether a day will come when he too (அடியேனும்) will know and praise. Tirumular states the knowing as done and as the Lord's gift; Arunagiri keeps it as a hope.

374 has the Lord pass from flesh, life and fire through the sun and moon until he stands as the whole universe (முழுதண்டமுமாகி). 2836 lists sea, wind, fire and space and says the one who stretches long and wide through earth and sky cannot be marked off. Both make the elements and the cosmos his extent rather than his boundary.

377 says the great being is felt ஊனத்தின் உள்ளே உயிர்போல், within the flesh like its life. 2324 reports what was seen ஊனிடை, within the flesh: the lord of knowledge, the light of a great gem and Shakti. The first states the presence in the body as doctrine, the second as something seen.

378 has the world embrace the supreme light that rose and walk around it (உலகம் வலம்வரும்), traditionally the linga. 2836 says the speaker does not know how to mark off (வரைந்து) the one who spreads through earth and sky so as to walk around him (வலம்செயுமாறு அறியேனே). Circling needs a bounded form; 2836 points out that what is circled is not bounded.

source_issues: 373: variant last line நானே அறிந்தேனென் ஆண்மையினாலே (by my own power) reverses the sense of the text's அவனாண்மையாலே (by his power).
377: variant கடலூழித் for கடல் வாழித் changes Vishnu's epithet.
378 and 380 are obscure in places (முங்கண், கோலிங்கமைஞ்சு; வீழித் தலைநீர்) and may be corrupt.
